items.a: After seeing many items that look fine, a single agent **assumes the rest are fine and stops checking**, so coverage silently drops.

items.q: Why shouldn't an agent grade its own work?
items.a: **Self-preferential bias**: the agent that wrote it tends to say it's good. Put review in a **separate, isolated context**.

items.q: How do you stop goal drift in long runs?
items.a: Copy the **original goal verbatim into every sub-agent** so compaction can't wash out rules like "don't touch prod".

items.q: What does a Flow actually do?
items.a: A **lead agent writes a phased plan**, then fans out to short-lived sub-agents, each owning one **discrete, verifiable unit of work**.

items.q: How do you keep a flow affordable?
items.a: Route a **cheap model to wide phases** (scan) and spend more compute on the hard phase (review), with a **budget** set.

items.q: Where should API keys live for agents?
items.a: Never in the sandbox: it sees fake values and the **real credential is injected at the egress proxy**, only for **allowlisted hosts**.

items.q: Why prefer auto mode over always-ask?
items.a: Humans approve about **97% of prompts on autopilot**; a model classifying each tool call is **more patient than you**.

items.q: What are the three developer jobs for agent safety?
items.a: **Declare** what the agent may do, **contain** what it can reach, and **detect** problems via the event stream.
